solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hoards, in a way, trophy for excelling in some tests

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

parts.words: trophy for excelling in some tests
parts.note: the Ashes is the trophy contested in England-Australia Test cricket series

explanation.surface: A sports trophy for doing well in test matches, kept somewhere as a hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the urn England and Australia play for in Test cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashes as a verb means hides away supplies, a synonym for hoards.

clue.text: Battles resistance in South-West town

indicators.note: the resistance letter is placed in the middle of the town's name

parts.note: St Ives is a town in Cornwall, in the south-west of England
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fights against opposition break out in a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, in England's far south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Strives as a verb means struggles or contends, as one battles against something.

clue.text: If held up in start, disorientated initially

indicators.note: the reversed pair sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
letters that are disorientated lose their positions and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuck right at the beginning is confused at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses IF to FI in this down entry, and 'disorientated' rearranges START to ATRST, with FI going in after AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the beginning, the same sense as the adverb initially.

clue.text: Like Wordsworth's daffodils, a showy plant

parts.note: Wordsworth's poem saw 'a host, of golden daffodils', so the daffodils were a host

explanation.surface: A flamboyant flower compared with the daffodils of Wordsworth's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth wrote 'I wandered lonely as a cloud', in which he sees 'a host, of golden daffodils'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a garden perennial grown for its large decorative leaves and flower spikes.

clue.text: Persevere as child protecting grandparent, for one? Right

indicators.note: the child word wraps around the other pieces to protect them

parts.note: a son is a child
an oldie is an old person, of whom a grandparent is an example

explanation.surface: A child looking after a grandparent is told to keep going, rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: An oldie is British slang for an elderly person; a grandparent is offered as one example, hence 'for one'.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom meaning to keep going despite difficulty, just as to persevere.

clue.text: Caught a programme about Conservative's source of profit

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the programme word goes around the Conservative letter

parts.note: a show is a broadcast programme
C is the abbreviation for Conservative; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A TV programme about the Tory party is caught out over its money-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOW wraps around C, after C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates money, an idiom for a dependable earner.

clue.text: Either cold or hot stuff, we hear, in this country

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that sounds like the one entered

parts.note: chilly means cold, and chilli is hot stuff; both sound the same

explanation.surface: A country where the weather or the food is either freezing or fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: Both CHILLY (cold) and CHILLI (hot pepper) sound like the country's name, hence 'Either'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is the long South American nation on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: One can't see the point of this device being used

definitions.text: One can't see the point of this device being used

parts.words: One can't see the point of this device being used
parts.note: when this fastener is closed its sharp tip is tucked away in a guard, so the point is hidden

explanation.surface: A gadget whose purpose seems lost on someone using it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see the point' looks like 'understand the purpose', but literally the sharp end is concealed when the pin is fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a bent pin whose point clasps into a covering cap when closed.

clue.text: Lab worker cut end off white garment

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its final letter

parts.note: a chemist works in a laboratory

indicators.note: the end taken off the next word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of white

explanation.surface: A laboratory worker trims the bottom of a white garment.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEMIST is cut to CHEMIS, then the end of 'white' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift or undergarment worn by women.

clue.text: Warning in advice about must-see film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colloquial caution, be careful
second meaning: literally telling someone to see a film

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is a gruff caution and a literal recommendation to view a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British colloquial caution, like 'mind out', and also literally urges someone to view something.

clue.text: No fur seal should be mistreated

indicators.note: letters that are mistreated are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal-welfare slogan saying no fur seal should suffer abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' looks like part of the slogan but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a refusal, a denial of a request.

clue.text: Change one's tone to pass on complaint about left

indicators.note: the word for spreading disease goes around the letter for left

parts.note: to infect is to pass on an illness, a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone shifts voice while grumbling about the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance but means an illness here.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect is to modulate the voice, varying its pitch.

clue.text: Enunciate Biblical piece about island

indicators.note: the scripture word goes around the island's name

parts.note: a verse is a numbered section of a chapter of the Bible
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: Read aloud a passage of scripture concerning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enunciate' suggests clear pronunciation, but the answer simply means putting into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To verbalise is to express in spoken words, a near synonym of enunciate.

clue.text: Temperature above normal in part of body

parts.note: high means above the usual level

explanation.surface: A fever reading somewhere on the body is higher than normal.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper leg between hip and knee.

clue.text: Action by those who won't stand for something?

definitions.text: Action by those who won't stand for something?

parts.words: Action by those who won't stand for something?
parts.note: protesters who refuse to tolerate a policy occupy a place by literally sitting down, not standing

explanation.surface: Protest by people who refuse to tolerate injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't stand for' means won't tolerate, but the protesters also literally stay seated.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Nothing can inspire such fear for very long

definitions.text: Nothing can inspire such fear for very long

parts.words: Nothing can inspire such fear for very long
parts.note: this dread is of novelty, and nothing stays novel for very long

explanation.surface: No terror can last long before it fades.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a comfort that fear fades, but the fear is of the new, and newness never lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is a dread of anything novel or unfamiliar.

clue.text: Person getting, in Rome, 2% off

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals, and % is read as per cent

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a two-percent discount while in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue's 2% the Roman way: II plus PERCENT, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient is one who receives, the person getting something.

clue.text: Something that may bounce, like ball in test, up and down

parts.note: a cheque bounces when the bank refuses it
the ball used in Test cricket is red

explanation.surface: A ball bouncing in a cricket match, rising and falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Test cricket uses a red ball; a cheque that bounces is refused for lack of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered history is one of mixed fortunes, with ups and downs, an idiom.

clue.text: Declare, for example, this clue devoid of content

parts.note: the word this is an example of a pronoun

indicators.note: a word devoid of content keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of clue

explanation.surface: A self-referential claim that this clue is empty of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the grammatical example: a demonstrative pronoun. CLUE emptied of its middle leaves CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to state formally or officially, as a verdict is declared.

clue.text: Took steps about love with female — it's looking serious

indicators.note: the walking word goes around the other two pieces

parts.note: paced means walked step by step
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A man paced around his beloved and a woman, looking grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a zero score in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced is a British colloquialism for solemn or humourlessly disapproving in expression.

clue.text: Giving go-ahead for vote accepted by old ruler

indicators.note: the vote word is taken inside the old ruler

parts.note: a king is a ruler
ay (aye) is a yes vote

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch approves something after a ballot is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aye' (also spelt AY) is the parliamentary yes vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Okaying is approving, giving permission for something to proceed.

clue.text: Skill put into speech? Not at all

indicators.note: putting a word into speech means saying it, so the entry sounds like it

parts.note: know-how is practical skill

explanation.surface: Expertise expressed in words turns out to be no use at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect adverb meaning in no way whatsoever.

clue.text: Shelter to put up for poor person

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A refuge built for someone in need.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'put up' means reversed, so TO becomes OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is a person lacking wealth, the opposite of the haves.

clue.text: What explodes we had placed around a rocket's front?

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the other pieces
the letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of rocket's

explanation.surface: A question about what we fitted to the nose of a rocket that blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed' rearranges WE HAD to WHEAD, which then goes around A plus R, the front of 'rocket's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive charge carried at the front of a missile.

clue.text: Be brilliant, briefly, and ostentatious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shine brightly for a moment

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is a short burst of light; the adjective is British slang for showy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to give a sudden burst of light, and as an adjective it is slang for showy or gaudy.

clue.text: Clear, subject to legal constraint

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ordered by a court to keep the peace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' suggests acquitted, the opposite of the legal sense; it means leaped across. In British law an offender bound over must keep the peace or forfeit money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound over something is to leap across it, and in law being bound over is a court order to behave.

clue.text: Volley from ring-leader trapped by police raid

indicators.note: the letter is trapped inside the raid word

parts.note: a bust is a police raid
the leader of ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of a criminal gang caught in a police swoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-leader' reads as a gang boss but just gives the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of gunfire is a volley, a rapid series of shots.

clue.text: One liable to quote scripture was shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: lived means existed, as was does

explanation.surface: Someone who quotes the Bible was exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's 'The devil can cite Scripture for his purpose' is the allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb from The Merchant of Venice says Satan can cite Scripture for his own purpose.

clue.text: E.g., Hillary Clinton, initially flexible

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of Clinton
limber means supple, flexible

explanation.surface: A description of Hillary Clinton as adaptable from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hillary Clinton' looks like the politician, but the definition is Edmund Hillary, first to scale Everest with Tenzing Norgay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edmund Hillary, the mountaineer, is an example of a mountain ascender.

clue.text: Something sweet returned, for example? Surely not!

indicators.note: returned means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: never is an exclamation of disbelief, surely not

explanation.surface: Someone is handed back a dessert and protests in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: EG plus NEVER, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'revenge is sweet' says getting even brings pleasure.

clue.text: Execute decoration, e.g. painting two-wheeled vehicle

parts.note: to do is to execute or carry out
GC is the George Cross, a British gallantry decoration
painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: Carry out decorating, such as painting a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross (GC) is a British award for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogcart is a light horse-drawn carriage with two wheels, once used to carry sporting dogs.

clue.text: What's done about cancelled service? It's taken out

indicators.note: the deed word goes around the tennis call

parts.note: a deed is something done
a let in tennis is a serve that is void and replayed

explanation.surface: A query about a service that was called off, which has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is retaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted means removed or struck out, as text is taken out.
